providers.title: Two-forms on an almost Hermitian four-manifold
providers.scope: In a unitary frame, F = e12 + e34 is self-dual of norm squared 2; the anti-invariant two-forms are self-dual; every unit complex-line bivector l is invariant with F(l) = 1, l^+ = F/2 and *l = F - l.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Invariant bivectors as Hermitian matrices
providers.scope: Invariant bivectors correspond to Hermitian 2 x 2 matrices with the trace inner product; v ^ Jv corresponds to z z*; those of nonnegative matrix and trace one are convex combinations t1 l1 + t2 l2 of complex lines of a unitary frame, of norm at most one with equality exactly for complex lines, and of rank two exactly in that case.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A closed lift of anti-invariant forms
providers.scope: With the projected elliptic operator R d d^* on anti-invariant forms, its kernel projection H and generalized inverse G, the order-zero operator B = d d^* G + H satisfies dB = 0 and RB = id.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Measure representation of positive functionals
providers.scope: A linear functional on two-forms that vanishes on anti-invariant forms, is nonnegative on semidefinite invariant forms and equals one on F is integration of alpha(l) against a probability measure on the unit complex-line bivectors, with trace measure and a polarization field.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The separating current
providers.scope: If no closed form is compatible with J, there are a positive current P annihilating closed invariant forms and a self-dual anti-invariant correction Q such that P + Q annihilates all closed forms.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Order zero on concentrated inputs
providers.scope: An operator of order zero on a closed four-manifold has kernel O(d^-4) off the diagonal, and maps a form supported in a ball of radius a with k-th derivatives at most M a^-k to a form bounded by CM.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Quadratic mass growth
providers.scope: The trace measure of the separating current satisfies mu(B_s(x)) <= C s^2 for all centres and radii.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The zero pairing
providers.scope: If T annihilates all closed forms and T' is a closed current, then <S_r T, * S_r T'> = 0 for the resolvent powers S_r = (1 + r^2 Delta)^-3.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The angular identity
providers.scope: For unit complex-line bivectors l at x and m at y and parallel transport tau, <l, * tau m> = |l - tau m|^2/2 - |F_x - tau F_y|^2/4.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The relative projection estimate
providers.scope: If a smooth orthogonal projection Pi annihilates a distribution W, then ||Pi S_r W|| <= C r ||S_r W||.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Square integrability and the angular bound
providers.scope: Under the heat kernel hypothesis (HK), the correction Q is square integrable, the angular integral is O(r^4), and the cross pairings of Q with every subcurrent of P tend to zero.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Closedness of the positive-density part
providers.scope: For a positive current on unit complex-line bivectors with a square integrable anti-invariant correction making it closed, quadratic mass growth and an O(r^4) angular bound imply that the density exists everywhere and that the restriction of the current to the points of positive density is closed.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Existence of the two-dimensional density
providers.scope: Under the hypotheses of the closedness theorem, r^-2 mu(B_r(p)) converges at every point, by an almost monotonicity formula of Lelong type.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Planar tangent measures and the transverse moment
providers.scope: At almost every point of positive density the polarization is a complex line and every tangent measure is a multiple of area on it; the mean-square transverse displacement is o(r^2).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tangential derivatives of density cutoffs
providers.scope: The derivatives of the smoothed densities along the complex lines of the current tend to zero in the mean, because closure converts them into the product of angular and transverse errors.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Taming implies compatibility
providers.scope: Under the heat kernel hypothesis (HK): an almost complex structure on a closed four-manifold that is tamed by a closed two-form admits a compatible closed two-form.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
